LESSON: FAMILY NEEDS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Environment
Topic 1.3: Family needs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Family needs, part of Social Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we choose the food we eat?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify basic needs in the family,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Family needs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Family needs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Family needs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: learner manipulates digital devices with assistive technology while recording poems and songs on different family

needs.

● Self-efficacy: learner sorts and groups locally assorted food items into types of tastes.

Values:
Respect: learner enhances patience for diverse opinions while sharing information on different family needs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: learner develops the skill of self-awareness when drawing, colouring, grouping different family needs.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Basic needs of the family such as water relates with filling and emptying activities in Mathematical Activities

Suggested Learning Resources

Digital devices with assistive technology, approved support learning materials, pictures, manilla papers, photographs, pencils and crayons,

food items, water, water container, houses, models of huts and manyatta, assorted clothings.
